authoring_notes.value: anchor: 'settlement_status' (custody-distinctive; the failed-status aging, NOT the settlement_fail label) routes this off a churn catalog.
borders/reads the fail outcome (POST-fail) — like a collections post-charge-off signal; observe strictly on pre-label observations for a prediction model.
OUTPUT additivity is measure-dependent: aged_fail_share is a non-additive ratio; mean_fail_age_days is a duration (n/a) — the default carries the ratio case.

business_interpretation.value: Fail-ageing buckets — how long already-FAILED instructions have been aging (measure=aged_fail_share in buckets, or mean fail_age_days), a POST-fail asset-servicing signal on the fail → buy-in tail.

eligibility_note.value: ⚠ NEAR-LABEL: build the signal from PRE-fail observations STRICTLY before the predicted instruction's settlement outcome (never the settlement_fail label itself — the engine refuses it; window ≠ the label window); the 3-part leakage control must FLAG it. fail-ageing is a POST-fail signal (the fail → buy-in tail) — for a fail-PREDICTION model observe it on PRIOR/other instructions, never the target instruction's own post-fail age. built from PRE-fail signals (settlement_status pending/failed history, settlement_cycle length), NEVER the settlement_fail outcome (a leakage anchor the engine refuses by construction).

point_in_time_declaration.value: point-in-time custody / settlement STATE observed as-of: the latest status / holding within (as_of − {window}, as_of], knowable strictly ≤ as_of, never forward. PIT-CRITICAL: a settlement outcome is not KNOWABLE until T+n (settlement_cycle) — honour system_time. DESIGN-TIME declaration — no data plane enforces runtime PIT.
